title: Paul, again
tomorrow: the Bible's last book has a dragon and plagues. what's the promise?

lines: A LOVE POEM INTO A FEUD?
cards: It turns up at weddings, on greeting cards, on wall art over the couch. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Charity is patient, is kind." Here's the odd part.
Paul didn't write it for a couple in love. He wrote it to a church in Corinth that was fighting: taking sides over favorite preachers, taking each other to court, showing off their spiritual gifts.
So why send a love poem into a feud?

teach.b: Because it's medicine, and every line names a symptom. Charity envies not: they were jealous over whose gift looked best. Charity is not puffed up: earlier in the same letter Paul says some of them are puffed up.
Charity seeks not her own: at their shared meal, some ate first and others went home hungry. Read that way, the poem is a mirror held up to a quarrel.
And look what comes first in the list. Not passion, not romance. Patient.

teach.h: AGAPE, CARITAS: A LOVE THAT GIVES.
teach.b: Charity, in the Douay, is the old word for agape in Greek and caritas in Latin, a love that gives. It isn't a donation. It's the love that waits for a slow brother and keeps showing up for a difficult sister.
The Corinthians prized their gifts, prophecy and tongues and knowledge. All of those, he says, will end.
Only one thing won't: "Charity never falleth away." Something to tell a friend tonight: that wedding reading was first read out loud to a congregation in the middle of a fight.
Which may be the best reason to read it at a wedding.

how: Catholics often choose 1 Corinthians 13 as a reading at weddings, and the Church names charity as the greatest of the three theological virtues, with faith and hope.

o: the apostle who wrote that charity is patient

the evangelist who wrote the fourth Gospel

games.q: the letter and the feud — tap the pairs.
p: agape, caritas: a love that gives

s: Paul wrote 1 Corinthians 13 for a wedding
he wrote it to a church fighting over preachers, lawsuits and gifts.
in the Douay-Rheims, 'charity' stands for agape, a love that gives
not a donation: caritas in Latin, agape in Greek.
Paul says spiritual gifts like prophecy last forever

games.q: two friends in your group chat are fighting over who got invited where, and you're tempted to pick a side. what's Paul's move with the Corinthians?
o: call both back to charity: patient, kind, not puffed up.
pick the side that's more right and say so plainly.
leave the group chat so you stay out of it.
games.why: Paul names the factions in Corinth, then holds up charity as the mirror: patient first, then kind.

practice: Read this out loud, slowly, the way you'd say it to someone you're short with lately: charity is patient, is kind. Then say that person's name, and the line once more.
Let the sit be patience practice: when you want it to be over, stay.

wordCard.voice: Paul. The apostle who wrote to a quarreling church that charity is patient and never falls away.

orig.note: Latin, 1 Corinthians 13:4 in the Vulgate: caritas patiens est, charity is patient.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: charity never falleth away, not even in the middle of a feud. See you tomorrow.
